title: Out-of-sample test of the second-order compensation residual, alpha_inter=0.3
purpose: Test whether the leading-order residual of perfectly balanced (mixed, equal-K) communities under near-perfect exposure correlation, R ~ kappa sigma_env^2 with kappa = sum(b^2) A_d^2 (1-c^2)/(1-phi^2), predicts simulated variability across richness, competition and environmental autocorrelation.
rationale: Predictions for every cell were computed before running and are stored in build/fable_sigma_check_2026-10-18/prespecified_predictions.json.
sigma_env 0.1 and 0.2 test the small-noise coefficient and its quadratic scaling; 0.5 and 1.0 test whether buffering erodes with fluctuation size beyond S=4, alpha_inter=0.3, phi=0.4.
Only independent and near-perfectly correlated exposures are needed for the endpoint ratio.
The alpha_inter=0.3, S=4, phi=0.4 cells replicate existing fig1_s4_highres_v1 cells with independent seeds.
acceptance_checks: The combined parquet validates against the manifest with 1000 replicates per scenario.
Floor occupancy is reported for every cell; cells with any floor contact are flagged, not dropped.

Prespecified success, applied to cells in the small-noise regime (predicted R at sigma_env=0.1 below 0.1): the observed balanced ratio at sigma_env=0.1 lies within 20% of the prediction, and R(0.2)/R(0.1) lies between 3 and 5 where the predicted R(0.2) is below 0.2. Cells with larger predicted values test saturation and are reported separately, with the expectation that the leading-order term over-predicts there.
